page: Microsoft Azure E32ns_v6 is an Env6-family virtual machine configured with 32 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the E32ns_v6 is designated as network-optimized and premium storage capable, though it does not feature any local SSD storage. This configuration relies entirely on remote storage solutions. The server does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, focusing its resource profile on high-capacity memory and network throughput.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in memory-intensive and parallel processing workloads. The server achieved a strong rating in large-block read-only memory bandwidth at 192.86 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 205.46 GB/sec. It also demonstrated strong capabilities in static web serving throughput at 56.03 GB/sec and Passmark CPU physics testing. In LLM inference benchmarks, it achieved a top-tier result of 381.68 tokens/sec for text generation with a small 135M model, and a strong 200.75 tokens/sec for prompt processing with a medium 7B model, though text generation on a large 70B model was poor at 2.56 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E32ns_v6 offers a dense memory-to-vCPU allocation suitable for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of local storage hardware. This makes it an appropriate fit for large-scale database hosting, in-memory caching, high-throughput web serving, and moderate machine learning inference tasks that leverage CPU-based matrix extensions.
description: The Microsoft Azure E32ns_v6 is an Env6-family virtual machine designed for memory-intensive and network-optimized workloads. It features 32 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz with 16 physical cores. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the server lacks local storage and GPUs but supports premium remote storage. Benchmark data highlights strong performance in large-block memory read bandwidth (192.86 GB/sec), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (205.46 GB/sec), and static web serving (56.03 GB/sec). It also excels in small-model LLM text generation, reaching 381.68 tokens/sec. This resource profile makes the E32ns_v6 highly suitable for in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
